summary: Repaired both owned scalar-typing census classes through the shared scalar paths, no per-operator branches. (1) The 176-row 'float scalar width 32 differs from its record width 64' class: the bundle record holds the host scalar at its own width (a Python float packs as a float64 record) while the kernel signature types the argument fp32 (pinned mangle_type); the widths are independent by construction, so the entry binding now CONVERTS on read instead of refusing -- scalar.py::convert_float_scalar emits the splat-convert-extract form (vfncvt.f.f.w RTNE narrowing / vfwcvt.f.f.v exact widening, stepwise 64<->32<->16, avl=1, the double-LMUL source view the probed no-overlap form uses); integer records keep the existing wide-form strunc (checked: no width-disagreement refusal exists on the integer path). The record load's ext tag for 64-bit records now uses the repertoire's single 64-bit row (sext, vacuous) so float64/uint64 records select. (2) The 90-row 'const: float width 16 is not in the scalar core' class: lower_const now materializes fp16/bf16 constants at their OWN width as the raw IEEE bits under the declared constant rounding (scalar.py::float_const_bits: fp16 via <e RTNE with IEEE inf on overflow; bf16 via the RTNE bit rounding of the IEEE single word -- the same algorithm constprop._round_float declares), and the two fp32-materialization workarounds (the const op's 16-bit special case and the broadcast's splat-at-fp32-and-round path) were removed so every consumer splats the pre-rounded bits directly with no second rounding. Filtered sweep over the 62 operators carrying the classes: both classes at ZERO (318 identities: 77 artifacts, up from 5; 241 refusals, all of other constructs). Executed evidence: a100c/tests/test_scalar_binding.py (new) -- bit-exact read-back of packed records at every binding width through compile->QEMU->compare (float64 record -> fp32 RTNE incl. negative zero sign bit and overflow-to-inf, float16/float32/int32/int64/uint32/uint64), fp16/bf16 constant rounding executed through masked-load other and tl.full, the census executors leaky_relu_kernel_strided (negative_slope) at 1/2/4/8 workers x 3 dtypes x 2 shapes and perf/leaky_relu, all under the cases' own policies; controls prove the checks distinguish conversion from re-read and RTNE from truncation. Full a100c suite (33 files incl. test_frontend_types.py) passes. Newly-exposed deeper failures were attributed to pre-existing defects outside this task's classes with controls (see remaining_work).

acceptance.observed: Both owned classes at ZERO: 'differs from its record width' rows = 0, 'float width 16 is not in the scalar core' rows = 0 (was 176 + 90 in the input census). 318 identities over the 62 operators: 77 artifacts (was 5) + 241 refusals, every refusal of a DIFFERENT construct (tl.dot 111, reduce 59, mir-verifier 28, ptradd 24, convert 9, allocation 6, tl.erf 4). Exit 1 comes only from the sweep's pre-existing 'refusals-located-and-countable' check: 2 allocation-class refusals (gemm_smallk float16) carry no source location -- the allocation class's own bookkeeping gap, identical in the input census (29 allocation rows there, 8 unlocated, 78 rows failing the same location pattern), unchanged by this task. All other sweep checks PASS incl. partition-sums (0 over-budget, 0 crash), repeat-cases-reuse-one-artifact (22 repeat cases, 0 violations -- no value baking: the record value is read and converted at run time), artifacts-are-riscv64-elf, enabled-pipeline-passes-on.

record-kind-matches-transport: the compiler's scalar_record_kind and the transport's own packer (a100_support.native_io.scalar) agree on (dtype, width) for every declared scalar record dtype (bool, int8..uint64, float16/32/64 -- one shared definition), and every kernel-signature type either matches its record width or the pair has a declared conversion. Executed read-back (pack a record, read it through the generated binding, compare bit-exact against numpy's own conversion): float64-record->fp32 (0.1 inexact, -0.1, -0.0 sign bit, 1e300 overflow-to-inf) at 1/2/4/8 workers; float16/float32/int32/int64/uint32/uint64 records. The conversion control records that the record's raw low half (0x9999999a) differs from the expected RTNE bits (0x3dcccccd), so a re-read instead of a conversion would fail.

fp16 constants lower at their own width with the declared RTNE (bits equal numpy fp16 casting for inexact/tie/overflow values; overflow is the IEEE infinity) and bf16 with the RTNE bit rounding of the single word (equal to an independent spec reference written in the test; the constprop fold's value re-encodes to the same bits -- one declared rounding); the truncation control differs so the checks are not vacuous. Executed: the masked-load other=0.1/0.5 constant is observable bit-exactly through an unmasked store at fp16 and bf16 (the matmul form), and tl.full at fp16/bf16 stores the rounded constant bit-exactly. Integer scalar widths bind without refusal (int64-record->int32 truncation, int32, int64, uint32, uint64 -- all executed bit-exact); the integer path has no width-disagreement refusal of the float class's shape.

remaining_work: Two-loop carried-value corruption (exposed, pre-existing, NOT this fix): a kernel whose body has TWO consecutive runtime loops (for off in range(0, N, TILE_N)) loses the value reduced after the first loop once the second loop is emitted -- rmsnorm_fwd_loop_kernel computes rsigma=1/sqrt(0+eps)=316.2278 instead of ~2.46. Minimal reproduction needs no scalar args and no 16-bit floats (sum-of-squares loop, then rsigma=1.0/tl.sqrt(var+1e-5) stored, then a second loop using rsigma): the second loop's emission zeroes the first loop's reduced value; the single-loop form executes exactly. Owner: the staging/liveout lane.

matmul column-32 defect (pre-existing): for EVEN_N=False tail tiles the whole last output column computes 0 (16 of 561 outputs at shape (17,33,100)); the float32 identity -- an artifact in the input census, on a path this task does not touch -- fails identically, so this is the dot/tile-mask lane's defect, newly reachable for the bfloat16 identity now that the const class no longer refuses it.

The allocation-class refusals carry no source location (2 rows in the filtered census; the input census shows the same gap on 29 allocation rows) -- the sweep's refusals-located-and-countable check fails on them; the allocation path should attach a loc like the other refusal paths.

Narrow integer/bool scalar ARGUMENTS (int8/uint8/int16/uint16/bool records) trip the grid wide-view smove (8/16 -> i64) at the MIR verifier -- the separate 'scalar widening' census class (4 rows, count_nonzero family); no corpus case binds them today, and the record packing itself is verified by this task's unit check.

The deeper census classes the owned identities now refuse at belong to their own repair tasks: tl.dot inside a runtime loop (111 rows), multi-width reduce (59), mir-verifier vsetvli-region at 16-bit (28), ptradd width (24), int64->f32 convert policy (9), allocation (6), tl.erf 16-bit (4).
